In addition to the [[2026–27 La Liga|domestic league]], Barcelona are participating in this season's editions of the [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] (entering for the [[FC Barcelona in international football#European Cup / Champions League|23rd consecutive season]]). They are also playing in the [[2026–27 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] and the [[2027 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]]. The season covers the period from 1 July 2026 until 30 June 2027. This is the first full season Barcelona are playing in their historic [[Camp Nou]] stadium since a hiatus of two full seasons during which the stadium was renovated and expanded.{{cite news |date=9 June 2025 |title=LaLiga marca el retorno al Spotify Camp Nou |trans-title=LaLiga marks its return to Spotify Camp Nou |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fc-barcelona/20250609/1002479943/laliga-marca-retorno-spotify-camp-nou.html |access-date=10 June 2025 |publisher=Mundo Deportivo |language=es |archive-date=6 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260806140707/https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fc-barcelona/20250609/1002479943/laliga-marca-retorno-spotify-camp-nou.html |url-status=live}} This is also the first season since [[2021–22 FC Barcelona season|2021–22]] without strikers [[Robert Lewandowski]], who departed the ''Blaugrana'' after his contract expired and joined [[Major League Soccer|MLS]] club [[Chicago Fire FC|Chicago Fire]], and [[Ferran Torres]], who departed the Catalan club to join French side [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]]. final|2015 Champions League]] title in the squad, and the first squad without a Champions League winner with Barcelona since the [[1997–98 FC Barcelona season|1997–98 season]]. ==Kits== |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4533239/barcas-2627-season-about-to-begin |title=Barça's 26/27 season about to begin |date=10 July 2026 |access-date=30 August 2026 week-long training camp in [[England]], based at [[St George's Park National Football Centre|St George's Park]] between 27 July and 3 August. On 23 June, Barcelona agreed the transfer of goalkeeper [[Iñaki Peña]] to [[Panathinaikos]] for €3 million, and exercised their purchase option to sign Egyptain forward [[Hamza Abdelkarim]] from [[Al Ahly]] on a permanent basis until 2029. A week later, [[Ansu Fati]]'s move to [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] was made permanent for €11 million, after Monaco triggered their buy option following his loan spell there. On 2 July, young winger [[Dani Rodríguez (footballer, born 2005)|Dani Rodríguez]] left permanently for [[Dinamo Zagreb]]. The following day, goalkeeper [[Diego Kochen]] was loaned to [[Lyngby Boldklub]]. On 17 July, young defender [[Andrés Cuenca]] completed a permanent move to [[Como 1907|Como]] for €500K. On 23 July, [[Karim Adeyemi]] arrived from [[Borussia Dortmund]] for a total fee of up to €29 million, reuniting with manager Hansi Flick, who gave him his [[German national football team|Germany]] debut. He signed a five-year deal. The next day, Barcelona opened preseason behind closed doors with a 4–1 win over Catalan side [[CE Europa|Europa]].{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4546260/training-continues-against-europa |title=Training continues against Europa |date=24 July 2026 |access-date=30 August 2026 |publisher=FC Barcelona |archive-date=2 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260802112755/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4546260/training-continues-against-europa |url-status=live}} On 29 July, Barcelona announced plans for a friendly against a local team in [[Tangier]], Morocco, scheduled for 15 August.{{cite news |title=FC Barcelona statement |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=29 July 2026 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/club/news/4549338/fc-barcelona-statement |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260729195357/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/club/news/4549338/fc-barcelona-statement |archive-date=29 July 2026 |url-status=live |access-date=25 September 2026}} Two days later, the club brought in Belgian teenage winger [[Jesse Bisiwu]] from [[Club Brugge]] for €8.5 million, signing him through 2031 primarily for the [[FC Barcelona B|reserve side]]. Later on, Barcelona played their first public friendly, drawing 2–2 away to [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] at [[St Andrew's Stadium|St Andrew's]]. Hamza Abdelkarim scored twice, but Barça lost the ensuing penalty shootout 3–2.{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/4551243/birmingham-city-2-2-3-2-fc-barcelona-preseason-opens-with-a-draw |title=Birmingham City 2-2 (3-2) FC Barcelona: Preseason opens with a draw |date=31 July 2026 |access-date=30 August 2026 |publisher=FC Barcelona |archive-date=30 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260830225641/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/4551243/birmingham-city-2-2-3-2-fc-barcelona-preseason-opens-with-a-draw |url-status=live}} ===August=== On 4 August, [[Marc-André ter Stegen]] was loaned to [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]]. The next day, centre-back [[Alexis Olmedo]] left permanently for [[RC Celta Fortuna|Celta Fortuna]]. On 6 August, Barcelona cancelled the planned friendly in Tangier, citing the [[2026 Ceuta migrant crisis|ongoing situation in Ceuta]] as making the match inappropriate.{{cite news |title=Friendly in 1–0 before losing to hosts [[Udinese]] by the same scoreline in a separate 45-minute fixture.{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4556439/second-in-the-triangular joined [[Liverpool FC|Liverpool]] on loan, with an option for Liverpool to make the move permanent next summer for €55 million. On 15 August, Barcelona sold [[Ferran Torres]] to [[Paris Saint-Germain]] for €48.5 million. The following day, a much stronger Barcelona side thrashed [[FC Basel|Basel]] 2–5 at [[St. Jakob-Park]]. Jesse Bisiwu scored twice off the bench, with further goals from Karim Adeyemi, Hamza Abdelkarim and a [[Lamine Yamal]] penalty.{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/4560597/fc-basel-2-5-fc-barcelona-five-at-sankt-jakob-park |title=FC Basel 2-5 FC Barcelona: Five at Sankt Jakob-Park |date=16 August 2026 |access-date=30 August 2026 |publisher=FC Barcelona |archive-date=30 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260830232039/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/4560597/fc-basel-2-5-fc-barcelona-five-at-sankt-jakob-park |url-status=live}} A day after that, young defender [[Jofre Torrents]] was transferred to Ajax for €6 million. On 18 August, [[Rodri]] completed a move from [[Manchester City]] for a total fee of up to €76.5 million. The [[2024 Ballon d'Or|Ballon d'Or]] winner signed a four-year contract. The next day, Barcelona closed out preseason with a 2–1 win over [[Al Ahly]] in the [[Joan Gamper Trophy]] at [[Camp Nou]]. Goals from Hamza Abdelkarim and [[Raphinha]] secured the win, with Anthony Gordon missing a late penalty.{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4562739/fc-barcelona-2-1-al-ahly-gamper-stays-at-home |title=FC Barcelona 2-1 Al Ahly: Gamper stays at home |date=19 August 2026 |access-date=30 August 2026 |publisher=FC Barcelona |archive-date=29 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260829210728/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4562739/fc-barcelona-2-1-al-ahly-gamper-stays-at-home |url-status=live}} On 20 August, [[João Cancelo]] returned to Barcelona on a permanent, free transfer after terminating his contract with [[Al Hilal SFC|Al Hilal]], signing until 2029 for his third spell at the club. On the same day, young goalkeeper [[Áron Yaakobishvili]] was loaned to [[UD Almería|Almería]]. The following day, midfielder [[Tommy Marqués]] moved to [[SC Braga|Braga]] for €12 million. On 23 August, Barcelona opened their [[La Liga]] title defence with a 0–5 win away against [[Elche CF|Elche]]. Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon made their official debuts, with the first scoring his first goal. Other goals came from Raphinha and [[Fermín López]].{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401882913 |title=Raphinha, Fermín López both score two each as Barcelona open campaign with 5-0 win |date=23 August 2026 |access-date=30 August 2026 |publisher=ESPN |archive-date=29 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260829181732/https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401882913 |url-status=live}} Four days later, Barcelona completed the signing of Croatian goalkeeper [[Dominik Livaković]] from [[Fenerbahçe]] for a total fee of €4 million, on a four-year deal through 2030. Later on, Barcelona beat [[Athletic Bilbao]] 2–0 at Camp Nou, with Raphinha and Fermín scoring. Rodri made his Barcelona debut off the bench.{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401882921 |title=Rodri debuts as Barcelona beat Athletic to continue hot start |date=27 August 2026 |access-date=30 August 2026 |publisher=ESPN |archive-date=29 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260829181732/https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401882921 |url-status=live}} On 29 August, [[Héctor Fort]] was transferred to [[Real Sociedad]] for €8.5 million. Two days later, Barcelona thrashed [[Rayo Vallecano]] 5–2 at Camp Nou. Raphinha and Lamine Yamal both scored braces to secure the victory.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401882903|title=Raphinha, Yamal doubles see Barcelona continue hot start|date=31 August 2026|access-date=31 August 2026|publisher=ESPN}} Hamza Abdelkarim came off the bench late in the second half to make his official debut for the club. ===September=== On 1 September, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Gabriel Jesus]] from [[Arsenal FC|Arsenal]] for a total fee of up to €14 million, signing a contract until 2029.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/49773859/gabriel-jesus-completes-transfer-barcelona-arsenal|title=Gabriel Jesus completes transfer to Barcelona from Arsenal|date=1 September 2026|access-date=1 September 2026|publisher=ESPN|archive-date=1 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260901234652/https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/49773859/gabriel-jesus-completes-transfer-barcelona-arsenal|url-status=live}} The club also confirmed the departures of [[Guille Fernández (footballer, born 2008)|Guille Fernández]] to [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] for €2.2 million and [[Álvaro Cortés]] to [[Royal Antwerp FC|Royal Antwerp]] for €3.5 million, while [[Toni Fernández]] and [[Marc Casadó]] joined [[Venezia FC|Venezia]] and [[Deportivo de A Coruña|Deportivo A Coruña]] respectively, both on loan. On 6 September, Barcelona secured a resounding 0–5 victory over [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] at the [[Mestalla]], with goals from Lamine Yamal (2), Raphinha, Fermín, and [[Pedri]].{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4572837/valencia-cf-0-5-fc-barcelona-high-five |title=Valencia CF 0-5 FC Barcelona: High five! |date=6 September 2026 |access-date=9 September 2026 |publisher=FC Barcelona |archive-date=8 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260908052107/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4572837/valencia-cf-0-5-fc-barcelona-high-five |url-status=live}} The match also featured Gabriel Jesus' official debut for the club. Three days later, in their opening [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] match, Barcelona defeated [[Feyenoord]] 5–1 at home, with Raphinha scoring twice, Lamine Yamal from a free-kick, Gabriel Jesus scoring his first goal for the club, and Karim Adeyemi also finding the net.{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4574250/fc-barcelona-5-1-feyenoord-dancing-in-the-rain |title=FC Barcelona 5-1 Feyenoord: Dancing in the rain |date=9 September 2026 |access-date=9 September 2026 |publisher=FC Barcelona |archive-date=10 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260910052551/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4574250/fc-barcelona-5-1-feyenoord-dancing-in-the-rain |url-status=live}} On 13 September, Barcelona defeated [[Levante UD|Levante]] 2–4 away, thanks to goals from Lamine Yamal (2), Adeyemi, and [[Xavi Espart]].{{cite news |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4575841/levante-2-4-fc-barcelona-the-wins-keep-coming |title=Levante 2-4 FC Barcelona: The wins keep coming |date=13 September 2026 |access-date=13 September 2026 |publisher=FC Barcelona |archive-date=14 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260914002113/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4575841/levante-2-4-fc-barcelona-the-wins-keep-coming |url-status=live}} The latter scored his first goal for the club. Three days later, Barcelona thrashed [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]] 7–2 at Camp Nou, with goals from João Cancelo, Raphinha (3), Gabriel Jesus and Lamine Yamal, as well as an own goal from [[Asier Villalibre]]. With this victory, Barcelona extended their winning streak to seven consecutive matches, setting a new club record for the best-ever start to a season.{{cite news |title=A first time for 7 from 7 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4577474/a-first-time-for-7-from-7 |date=16 September 2026 |access-date=16 September 2026 |publisher=FC Barcelona |archive-date=17 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260917042040/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/4577474/a-first-time-for-7-from-7 |url-status=live}} Barcelona concluded the month on 19 September due to the [[FIFA International Match Calendar|FIFA international break]], with a 1–3 away win against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], thanks to a [[Hat-trick#Perfect hat-trick|perfect hat-trick]] from Raphinha.
